name: Beatrice Ko
life: “I still remember a pan that sat at an angle on our first hob.” People around Harbour Bakery know Beatrice by a small Tuesday habit. Beatrice buys one familiar thing and asks who chose the unfamiliar thing in the window.
voice: I chose a saucepan with a dent from my first flat. Its note is flatter than any kitchen I have now.
appearance: Beatrice is easy to recognize by a smooth side part with one rebellious curl and a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Usually dressed in a long navy raincoat with a pen clipped inside the neckline, Beatrice listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Beatrice is kind in very practical ways and prickly about being thanked in public. Beatrice loves being recognized by the people who notice what happens after the guests have left.
agenda: To play the saucepan's actual imperfect pitch.
family: Sol Lane is Beatrice’s parent’s cousin. Beatrice chooses the music. Sol puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The small signature*, Sol says, “My wife and I used to play chess with bottle caps here.”
connections: Kate Dinh. A dented saucepan and a typewriter find neighboring places in the same score.

reactions.situation: An instrument breaks before the fountain piece begins
reactions.response: Beatrice asks the player whether a different everyday object can carry the missing note.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Beatrice keeps the neighbor's place and finds out whether the stranger needs a different kind of help.
